topic: Upapada Lagna and the 2nd from it — the classical marriage-durability method (DD deep-dive reel, English, 2026-09-07 pm)

slides.sub: The classical marriage point — and why the 2nd from it is the part that matters

slides.body:
An Arudha (a reflection point — how a house shows up in the visible world, rather than what it truly is) is calculated for any house.

Upapada Lagna, usually written UL, is the Arudha of the 12th house. The 12th is the house of letting go — and in this tradition, the visible image of what you give away becomes the image of your marriage.

points: Find the 12th house from your Lagna (ascendant)
Find its lord and count how far that lord has travelled
Count the same distance again from the lord — that sign is the Arudha
If it lands on the 12th itself or the 6th from it, take the 10th from that instead
The sign you end on is the Upapada Lagna

slides.body:
This is the step that gets skipped. Classical texts read the 2nd house counted from the Upapada Lagna for the sustenance of the marriage — whether the bond holds its shape over time.

The logic is the same one used everywhere else in Jyotish: the 2nd from any house is that house's maraka and its nourishment at once. What feeds a thing is also what can end it.

points: Benefics in or aspecting the 2nd from UL — traditionally supportive
Malefics there — read as strain, not as verdict
The lord of the 2nd from UL and its dignity
The UL lord itself — strong, weak, combust, well-placed
Cross-check in Navamsa (the D9 divisional chart, the marriage varga)
And always the running dasha — timing lives there, nowhere else

slides.body:
UL is one technique inside a large system, and the Arudha methods come from the Jaimini stream — respected, but not the only lens. A difficult 2nd from UL is a flag to read further, never a prediction of separation.

Astrologers who announce divorce from this single placement are misusing it. No single point in a chart decides a marriage, and no honest reading of this method produces a guarantee in either direction.

Comment if this one was new to you — most readings never get past the 7th house, and the 2nd from UL is where the classical method actually lives.

Save this for the next time you sit with a chart, and follow along.
